correctness_confidence.basis: Every theorem and proof checks out from first principles: Wedderburn-Artin plus discriminant-free Minkowski packing (Thm 2.1), Hessenberg cycle expansion and IVT/residue peeling (Thm 3.1), Landau-Ramanujan and Ford bounds (Thm 4.1), Jacobi matching peeling, sharp d=2 parity threshold, spectral energy (Thm 4.2), and finite-field bounds/cones (Thms 5.1-5.2). Only minor notational and figure-labeling slips occur.

rigor.basis: Clear definitions, self-contained Lemmas 2.2 and 3.2, clean separation of analytical proofs from Lean-checked cores, and informative Table 1 and Figures 1-2. Minor editorial fixes are needed for B_0 subset K_0 in Thm 5.2(c), the d=3 Max commuting ceiling label in Fig 2(b), and Table 1 row 9 omitting the even-d qualifier.

novelty.basis: Initiates Spectral Sidon Sets in matrix algebras and establishes genuine non-commutative packing advantages, exact exponents in M_d([0,N]), a Landau-Ramanujan arithmetic obstruction in Sym_2([0,N]), Jacobi-band constructions, and super-exponential Galois-torus separation over F_p.

significance.basis: As a newly formulated problem bridging non-commutative matrix algebras, additive combinatorics, and analytic/algebraic number theory with open symmetric gaps, it is strong original research rather than a historic field-wide breakthrough.

reproducibility.basis: Explicit finite-field witness tuples in Sym_2(F_q) and Sym_3(F_q), exact constants c_d and c_d^sym, and SHA-256 digests are provided in the PDF. Under PDF-only review, all six finite-field witnesses, Hessenberg/Jacobi polynomial identities, and factorial dominance thresholds pass direct recalculation.

summary: This paper initiates the study of Spectral Sidon Sets in matrix algebras M_d(R), where pairwise sums A+B must have distinct characteristic polynomials. First-principles auditing confirms all six core results: (1) a sharp O_d(N^{d/2}) ceiling for all commuting integer families (including non-normal/nilpotent ones) via Wedderburn-Artin and discriminant-free Minkowski packing; (2) the exact optimal exponent sigma_d(N) = Theta_d(N^{d(d+1)/4}) for d >= 2 via a Hierarchical Hessenberg Spectral Decoding Theorem; (3) a strict separation sigma_2^sym(N) <= O(N^{3/2}/(log N)^{1/4}) = o(sigma_2(N)) from Landau sum-of-two-squares density and a Ford multiplication-table barrier in the equal-diagonal hyperbolic subspace; (4) a symmetric Jacobi-band lower bound Omega_d(N^{(3d-1)/4}), an exact d=2 rectangular parity injectivity threshold at u <= sqrt(N), and spectral additive energy bounds showing uniform probabilistic alteration stalls at Omega(N/(log N)^{1/3}); (5) char-2 collapse, exact odd-q d=2 commuting ceilings, and explicit Sym_2/Sym_3 non-commutative witnesses; and (6) super-exponential split-vs-elliptic torus separation over F_p via normal-basis cyclic cones. All proofs are sound with zero material objections; only minor notational/labeling slips require cleanup.
strengths: Thm 2.1 resolves commuting non-normal/nilpotent matrix families in M_d([0,N]) cleanly by combining Wedderburn-Artin composition-series multiplicities with a discriminant-free Minkowski l_infty-packing bound.

Thm 3.1 achieves the exact information-theoretic exponent d(d+1)/4 for every d >= 2 using an exact 2^{d-1}-term Hessenberg interval-cycle expansion, IVT root isolation, and zero-error superdiagonal residue peeling.
Thm 4.1 uncovers an authentic number-theoretic obstruction in Sym_2([0,N]) via Landau sum-of-two-squares parity splitting and an Erdos-Ford multiplication-table barrier in H_2^hyp([0,N]).
Thm 4.2 combines Jacobi matching-polynomial peeling (Omega_d(N^{(3d-1)/4})), a tight d=2 parity threshold u <= sqrt(N) with explicit collisions at u = 2k, and Ramanujan r_2^2 spectral-energy bounds.

Thms 5.1-5.2 establish char-2 collapse, exact d=2 finite-field commuting ceilings, independently verifiable Sym_2/Sym_3 witnesses, and super-exponential normal-basis elliptic-torus separation over F_p.
weaknesses: The paper initiates its own problem class rather than resolving an established open conjecture, and substantial asymptotic gaps remain for symmetric matrices: [N^{5/4}, N^{3/2}/(log N)^{1/4}] at d=2 and [N^{(3d-1)/4}, N^{d(d+1)/4}] for d >= 3.

In Thm 5.1(b), the elliptic-torus commuting lower bound >= q/7 leaves a constant factor gap to the exact ceiling q and omits characteristic p = 3, while Thm 5.1(c) provides only small-q witnesses without an asymptotic family beating q.

The Hessenberg and Jacobi decoding boxes require N >= max(8d, ceil(2/c_d)) with doubly-exponentially small c_d in d, so non-trivial asymptotic constants are deferred to O_d(.), and the d=2..5 numerical verification constants in Remark 3.5 rely on empirical recovery rather than the general theorem.
potential_errors: In Thm 5.2(c), B_0 is written as a subset of K_0, although K_0 in Part (b) was truncated at p' - 1 (largest odd prime <= (p-1)/2) rather than floor((p-1)/2) (e.g., p=17 gives p'-1=6 < 8); the proof of (c) works directly on B_0 without K_0, so no mathematical gap arises. Also p >= 9 should read p >= 11 for primes.

In Fig 2(b), the grey bars for Sym_3(F_3) (height 4) and Sym_3(F_5) (height 9) are labeled Max commuting ceiling / maximum commuting ceilings of Theorem 5.1, whereas they plot max(split, elliptic) and omit the mixed commuting torus F_q x F_{q^2} (counting ceilings 5 and 11, still beaten by the witnesses 6 and 12). Thm 5.1(c) text itself is accurate.

In Table 1 row 9, the elliptic lower bound (1-o(1))/(d*2^{d/2}) p^{d/2} omits the qualifier that it is proved only for even d >= 2 (odd d >= 25 uses (1-o(1))/(8*8^{d/2}) p^{d/2}), and the split upper bound omits + O_d(p^{d/2-1}).

In Thm 2.1(a), the strict inequalities M^2/2 < C(M+1,2) and (M-1)^2/2 < C(M,2) fail at M=0 (and M <= 1 for weak), though the stated upper bounds hold trivially there; in Thm 4.2(a) Stage 1, E(t) from (5) enters P(t) = B(t) - chi_S(t) with a minus sign, leaving |E(s_i)|/|D_i| < 1/2 unchanged.
strong_novelty_candidates: Spectral Sidon Sets in matrix algebras and the non-commutative packing jump from O_d(N^{d/2}) (for all commuting families including nilpotent ones) to Theta_d(N^{d(d+1)/4}).
Hierarchical Hessenberg Spectral Decoding Theorem (Lemmas 3.2-3.4) giving exact global injectivity of chi_S on full-scale upper-Hessenberg integer boxes.
Landau-Ramanujan symmetric-vs-non-symmetric arithmetic separation in Sym_2([0,N]) and Ford multiplication-table obstruction in H_2^hyp([0,N]).
Normal-basis cyclic-cone Galois-torus embedding (Thm 5.2) giving super-exponential separation of elliptic tori over split diagonalizable families in M_d(F_p).
